name: Akta Benchmarks 01
description: A four-cell benchmark band in the akta design language: each metric gets the graphic form its data actually asks for — an isometric bar city for a blowout, a hundred-unit comb for a tight cluster, a polar ring plot for a near-miss, and a stacked slab tower for a cost ratio — so no shared bar list flattens four different stories into one shape. Every figure is drawn from its own value, every chart ships a screen-reader table, and the whole thing is one file of Tailwind arbitrary values with dark twins.

variations.previewHint: Scroll the band into view — header and cells fade up on a view-timeline. Hover any bar, dot or slab for its provider and value.
variations.description: Four benchmark readouts on the 1440 grid, separated by hairline rules and corner notches rather than cards. F1 is an isometric bar city, accuracy a hundred-unit comb, coverage a polar ring plot, and cost a stack of slabs whose thickness is price. Each cell leads with the brand figure in mono display type, and blue is spent only on the one row the section is about.

features: Four graphic forms, one per metric: 2:1 dimetric bars for the F1 blowout, a 100-unit comb for the accuracy cluster, a polar ring plot for the coverage near-miss, and stacked slabs for the cost ratio
Every chart SVG shares a 330-unit viewBox width and a 330px cap, so SVG text renders at the same 12px as the HTML mono labels in every cell
Isometric faces recede toward the canvas via color-mix rather than toward a darker step, so the shading survives the brand ramp inverting in dark mode
Chart fills and strokes are fill-[…] / stroke-[…] utilities with dark twins — no inline var() and nothing written into globals.css beyond the notch and reveal device classes
The radar starts its radial scale at 40% and draws labelled grid rings, so the truncation is stated on the chart instead of hidden in it
Every drawn form ships a visually-hidden list of name: value pairs, so the screen reader gets data where sighted readers get a picture
Cells separate with a right+bottom inset-shadow rule, so the grid keeps dividing correctly at one, two or four columns
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — the scroll reveal only runs where a view-timeline is supported and motion is allowed
